sentences.text: This creature was a relatively small animal, reaching a total length of about 2.5 meters.
Its head was small and triangular, measuring 22.2 centimeters in length and 13 centimeters in width.
A distinctive feature of this animal is the presence of three crests on its skull.
The premaxilla bone bears a dental rosette containing five tooth sockets.
Teeth in positions four through six were very large, while the remaining teeth were smaller and more gracile.
Another opalized specimen, cataloged as SAM P2381, was found in the Andamooka opal fields.
The crests were likely covered in keratin, making them considerably taller than the bone alone suggests.
The holotype was discovered by local miners in the Zorba Extension Opal Field near Coober Pedy.
This specimen was purchased in 1988 by the chairman of Comrealty, Mr. Sid Londish.
All known specimens come from the Bulldog Shale in the Eromanga Basin of South Australia.
Researchers suggest the crests were likely used for communication rather than defense or combat because they were too delicate for those functions.
The animal was capable of tolerating the cold conditions of its polar habitat.
The genus of this animal is Umoonasaurus.
The only known species of Umoonasaurus is U. demoscyllus.
The parent group of Umoonasaurus is the family Leptocleididae.
Umoonasaurus is classified as a plesiosaur.
In 2008, Smith and Dyke reclassified Umoonasaurus as a member of Leptocleididae within Pliosauroidea.
In 2010, Ketchum and Benson placed Umoonasaurus in Leptocleididae, which they classified within Plesiosauroidea.
The time range for Umoonasaurus is from the Aptian to the Albian, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
The sea where Umoonasaurus lived was located at approximately 70 degrees South latitude in the polar regions.
